definitions.staleness_event: A connection attempt or liveness probe that resolves or targets an expired/dead endpoint while the peer is reachable at a newer state.
definitions.failed_connect: A browser-to-browser connection attempt that fails to open an ordered WebRTC DataChannel and complete 10 consecutive heartbeats within 10.0 seconds.

C1.note: Requires N>=30 live trials across distinct physical network pairs (home<->mobile, home<->cloud) with TURN disabled.

C2.note: Browser fetch/DoH cannot inspect OS/ISP recursive cache state directly without authoritative DNS write credentials + epoch subdomain probes.

C3.note: At equal refresh budget (B=30), Poisson/Entropy schedulers lose to Fixed-Interval under uniform/stationary churn and only win when churn is regime-switching.

C4.note: Periodic drops (CV=0.0) violate exponential memorylessness [0.5, 2.0]; requires Weibull/regime model for bursty network drops.

C5.note: Browsers cannot speak BGP (TCP 179 / WireGuard); requires external DN42 Linux daemon running BIRD/FRR.

C6.note: WebRTC ICE exchange requires at least a transient signaling relay (e.g. ntfy.sh) or DNS TXT dynamic update; pure static pages without a relay cannot exchange SDP.

C7.note: Illustrative layer timescales are configuration, not a measured separation guarantee; browsers do not speak BGP.

C8.note: Signature round trips and full content digests are tested. Latency and ownership trust require separate evidence; session-key self-verification is not authority.

C9.note: No browser BGP implementation; overlay discovery and peer/relay transfers only.

C10.note: Full object roots are never truncated. DNS serialization has explicit size bounds; bulk data remains at peers or an explicitly enabled public relay.

prism_model.scope: Pure admission, reconstruction relations and deterministic computation. Host bytes, crypto, clocks, peer assertions and network effects have explicit boundaries.
